identification.source_of_variation: None designed: an observational register cohort. Identification rests on sequential randomization (all common causes of the depression-dissolution association measured and adjusted for at each of the five annual time-points) together with positivity, with LTMLE used to estimate counterfactual risks under dynamic antidepressant-treatment regimes.

key_assumptions.assumption: Sequential randomization (no unmeasured confounding at any time-point): at each time-point all common causes of the depression-dissolution association are observed and controlled for
key_assumptions.supported_by: No test is offered. The authors argue they included 'a sufficient but not overly rich set of covariates' -- baseline covariates plus time-dependent education, income, civil status, joint children, psychiatric comorbidity, antidepressant class, Nordic Multimorbidity Index and oral contraceptives -- and concede that some important covariates may have been omitted.

heterogeneity.dimension: sex of the person suffering from depression (female vs male)
heterogeneity.finding: Marginally higher risk of family dissolution when men presented with depression than when women did, but the difference was not statistically significant (Fig. 5). Absolute risks at 1 year since formation: 42.0 % (38.2-45.8) for women (N = 9,667) and 43.3 % (39.6-47.0) for men (N = 4,886); at 5 years: 35.6 % (29.7-41.5) for women (N = 17,433) and 35.8 % (30.0-41.5) for men (N = 10,178).

heterogeneity.dimension: hospital-based care for depression (ever vs never)
heterogeneity.finding: Families in which a person received hospital-based care for depression carried excess risk of dissolution (Fig. A2); absolute risk 46.1 % (95 % CI 39.2-52.9 %) for hospital-based care in the first year and 38.2 % (95 % CI 34.9-42.5 %) in the fifth year after formation.

heterogeneity.dimension: presence of children in the family at depression onset
heterogeneity.finding: No statistical differences between the depression-induced dissolution risk in families with and without children, regardless of depression ascertainment (Fig. A3); a non-significant tendency towards higher dissolution risk in families without children.

register_source.value: The Danish National Prescription Registry: redeemed antidepressant drugs (ATC: N06A), annual yes/no indicator for either partner

definition.value: Dynamic regime: either partner has annual indicators of redeemed antidepressant drugs (ATC: N06A) in at least 5 consecutive annual periods during the 5 years of follow-up. Contrasted with the regime of no depressive episodes. The duration regimes are nested: families with at least k coherent years also had at least k-1 coherent years.

timing.value: Consecutive annual time-points within the 5 years of follow-up from the anchor year.

register_source.value: Statistic Denmark's population register: family ID (dissolution identified by discrepancy between the partners' family IDs at the end of each year)

definition.value: Indicator (yes/no) of family dissolution, defined as the discontinuation of a shared residential address for the two adults who constituted the family, identified by a change and discrepancy between each partner's family IDs at the end of each year; the estimated quantity is the covariate-adjusted absolute risk of dissolution at the end of 5 years of follow-up. Annual resolution only.

timing.value: At end of follow-up, i.e. 5 annual time-points after the anchor year (the second year after family formation); families are also censored at emigration or death of either partner.

units.value: percentage points (absolute excess risk of family dissolution at end of 5-year follow-up, versus the no-depression regime)

magnitude.interpretation: 'Prolonged depressive episodes carried greater risk of family dissolution than shorter episodes'

estimand.target_population: All newly-formed Danish families in the cohort: opposite-sex couples (married or cohabiting, with or without children) formed in 2008 or 2009, both partners aged 20-60, who had not dissolved by the end of the following year. heterogeneity.dimension: sex of the person suffering from depression (female vs male)
heterogeneity.finding: Marginally higher risk of family dissolution when men presented with depression than when women did, but the difference was not statistically significant (Fig. 5). Absolute risks at 1 year since formation: 42.0 % (38.2-45.8) for women (N = 9,667) and 43.3 % (39.6-47.0) for men (N = 4,886); at 5 years: 35.6 % (29.7-41.5) for women (N = 17,433) and 35.8 % (30.0-41.5) for men (N = 10,178).

heterogeneity.dimension: hospital-based care for depression (ever vs never)
heterogeneity.finding: Families in which a person received hospital-based care for depression carried excess risk of dissolution (Fig. A2); absolute risk 46.1 % (95 % CI 39.2-52.9 %) for hospital-based care in the first year and 38.2 % (95 % CI 34.9-42.5 %) in the fifth year after formation.

heterogeneity.dimension: presence of children in the family at depression onset
heterogeneity.finding: No statistical differences between the depression-induced dissolution risk in families with and without children, regardless of depression ascertainment (Fig. A3); a non-significant tendency towards higher dissolution risk in families without children.

heterogeneity.dimension: sex of the person suffering from depression (female vs male)
heterogeneity.finding: Marginally higher risk of family dissolution when men presented with depression than when women did, but the difference was not statistically significant (Fig. 5). Absolute risks at 1 year since formation: 42.0 % (38.2-45.8) for women (N = 9,667) and 43.3 % (39.6-47.0) for men (N = 4,886); at 5 years: 35.6 % (29.7-41.5) for women (N = 17,433) and 35.8 % (30.0-41.5) for men (N = 10,178).

heterogeneity.dimension: hospital-based care for depression (ever vs never)
heterogeneity.finding: Families in which a person received hospital-based care for depression carried excess risk of dissolution (Fig. A2); absolute risk 46.1 % (95 % CI 39.2-52.9 %) for hospital-based care in the first year and 38.2 % (95 % CI 34.9-42.5 %) in the fifth year after formation.

heterogeneity.dimension: presence of children in the family at depression onset
heterogeneity.finding: No statistical differences between the depression-induced dissolution risk in families with and without children, regardless of depression ascertainment (Fig. A3); a non-significant tendency towards higher dissolution risk in families without children.
